status: Closed — fixed in close transaction recovery status lane
finding: `taskflow close --write` can exceed the caller timeout after it has already mutated the live ledger, updated the planning mirror, and created both target/planning commits, leaving the operator with no final JSON response and forcing manual triangulation to learn whether retrying would duplicate or corrupt closeback state.
expectedBehavior: Long close transactions should either complete within the default operator timeout, stream/checkpoint durable progress, or expose a first-class `taskflow close-status` / recovery receipt that tells the operator whether ledger close, target commit, and planning commit already landed.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0277: `node atm.mjs taskflow close --task ATM-GOV-0277 --actor codex-skl-captain --historical-delivery 0b0918c3bfc14d90a68b51738d0e5f433f895858 --write --json` timed out at the caller after about 34 seconds. Read-only follow-up showed live ledger status `done`, planning frontmatter `done`, framework close commit `2a7c4b4d6`, and 3KLife planning close commit `26b046b0` already existed. Fixed in commits `e375ae4883` and `1411b25035`: taskflow close now persists an `atm.closeTransactionStatus.v1` receipt under `.atm/runtime/close-transactions/<task>.json`, records `started` and `ledger-written` phases, and exposes `node atm.mjs taskflow status --task <id> --json` as a read-only recovery query. Focused receipt test, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `git diff --check`, encoding guard, frozen runner build, and governed pre-push all passed.
followUp: Keep target/planning commit phase updates wired into future close orchestration changes; the durable status receipt is now the first recovery command after a caller timeout. Formal lifecycle cleanup of historical close receipts remains a separate governance decision.
